chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musanna, from Fitr ibn Khaleefa, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father, may the prayers of Allah be upon them, said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: Rasool Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever repels from a group of Muslims an adversity of water or fire, Paradise is obligated for him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for protecting Muslims from water and fire?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of the Ahl al-Bayt in al-Kafi, emphasizes the communal obligation (fard kifaya) of safeguarding the Muslim community from specific natural adversities like water and fire. It underscores the spiritual merit of proactive protection, promising Paradise to the individual who successfully repels these dangers, reflecting the Shia emphasis on practical service to the Ummah as a path to divine reward.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al hakam, from Musanna, from Fitr Bin Khaleefa, 
(It has been narrated) from Muhammad son of Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>, from his<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who repels from a group of Muslims, an adversity of water, or fire, the Paradise is Obligated for him’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Muthanna’ from Fitr ibn Khalifah from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Al-Husayn from his father, recipients of divine supreme covenant, who has said the following: “’Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, “If one defends a community of Muslims in the matters of their water or fire, paradise becomes necessary (allotted) for him.’”
